content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles, especially when sentiment is bullish.", "Sentiment spikes often precede sharp price drops, indicating model lag in capturing sentiment-driven reversals.", "Model forecasts show mean-reversion bias in later periods, underestimating sustained price declines.", "High sentiment positivity correlates with forecast overshoots, suggesting sentiment amplifies model errors.", "Price corrections after forecast peaks are more pronounced when sentiment turns negative.", "Models fail to anticipate sudden price spikes triggered by sentiment shifts, especially in late cycles.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with historical price patterns, indicating sentiment calibration is critical.", "Late-cycle forecasts are systematically too high, suggesting models overreact to recent volatility without adjusting for mean reversion."]}
